lines: +# PR #1 review and cc-safety-net coverage comparison
+Prepared against agent-config commit `f31b4ef3b6d934bf1c32feb0e6b640e7ecca8a87`,
+cc-safety-net 2.6.11 at `0626be7a791c17a0daa67ae90a899372c667056d`, and its official
+rulebooks at `d1fc329f00f1c8068f0ce57a855508043981f7c7`.
+The objective remains a classifier/decision-model layer above the hooks, with
+deterministic hooks owning hard denials, the model only asking for confirmation,
+and unavailable model results falling back to the host's normal permission flow.
+Broad guard-family coverage is already present. Reproducing an entire safety-net
+product or implementing complete Bash semantics would move beyond that objective.
+The PR had six unresolved review threads when inspected. They were addressed on
+the same branch in `f31b4ef`: S3 sync deletion; forced branch creation/reset;
+forced branch reset/move/copy; forced tag replacement; update-ref stdin
+transactions; and full-line redaction of unquoted prose passphrases. The newer
+`a7639cc` changes to executed SQL strings and rsync link options were retained.
+All 12 guard test scripts passed. The transaction tests passed again after the
+final stdin-versus-filename controls. New lint diagnostics: none. Type checking
+the touched runtime modules still reports two existing nullable-Git diagnostics
+in unchanged loops in dangerous_git.py; those are not new runtime failures.
+## What is covered
+| Area | cc-safety-net | Current hooks | Assessment |

+| Destructive Git | 26 named core entries: discards, force push, ref deletion, stash loss, worktree removal, overrides | Matching operation families in dangerous_git; some local removals ask; new force branch/tag and stdin-ref checks extend this | Broad family coverage, with different decision policies; not proof of every spelling |

+| Filesystem destruction | 15 named core entries: dangerous rm targets, find deletion, devices, formatting, shredding | rm_rf_guard asks for recursive forced rm; dangerous_system and config_guard cover devices, deletion and protected config | Broad coverage; ours prompts on some project/temp deletions upstream allows |

+| Nested execution | 11 named core execution entries: shell/interpreter nesting, awk, xargs, parallel, dynamic sources | Shared shell parser, wrappers, scripts, Make/package sources, interpreter strings and model routing | Strong static handling; incomplete/dynamic analysis still has gaps |

+| Secret access | Basenames, extensions, home credential trees and coding-CLI paths; shell and file-tool input | secrets_guard handles these families and nested/interpreter references; judge_redact protects model-bound context | Significant overlap; exact credential-path and tool-adapter parity has not been exhaustively measured |

+| Self-protection | Own policy/application guard and general Git metadata protection | Wider agent-config coverage across Claude, Codex, omp/pi, opencode and persistence locations | Different protected assets; general Git metadata coverage is not identical |
+| Cloud/IaC | Four opt-in official rulebooks, 50 rules | Terraform, AWS, gcloud and Azure tables, plus generic deletion rules | All 81 upstream block-labelled pack fixtures intercepted |

+| Additional controls | Built-in core and extensible rulebooks | SQL/database, Kubernetes/container, publishing, fetch-and-execute, security-control and persistence checks | Our deterministic scope already extends beyond upstream core |

+| Model decisions | The runtime gate is deterministic allow/deny; no network model classifier was found in the inspected gate | Optional Jev/AI Gateway decision models with typed concerns, contextual prompts, thresholds and redaction | This is the main intended differentiator |

+| Policy/platform product | Standard/Strict/Paranoid presets, custom rulebooks, shared policy, GUI, many hosts, Windows shells | Fixed Python tables, tiers, environment settings, Claude/omp/pi integration, Linux/macOS Bash | Product parity is unnecessary; PowerShell/CMD remain outside this PR |
+The named core counts describe upstream metadata entries, not a percentage of
+equivalent implementation. Eighteen other entries are PowerShell/CMD-specific.
+The official cloud packs are a separate repository; they are not all enabled by
+cc-safety-net's default core policy.
+## Measured replay
+I replayed all 6,965 upstream harvested literals through the four local
+deterministic hooks, then checked model eligibility only for deferred commands.
+The saved comparison column is `work/standard`; local checks used an empty
+workspace, default/high policy, and normal interactive permission mode. No
+literal was executed, no decision model was called, and there were no guard
+exceptions. Reproduce from this checkout with
+[`scripts/replay_ccsafety.py`](../scripts/replay_ccsafety.py); the upstream
+checkout is not vendored, so clone it at the pinned commit first:
+git clone https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net.git scratchpad/cc-safety-net
+git -C scratchpad/cc-safety-net checkout 0626be7a791c17a0daa67ae90a899372c667056d
+python3 scripts/replay_ccsafety.py
+Re-run on 2026-10-15 at claude-code-rules `a8d7345` (agent-config `d3d89bb`),
+the deny-labelled row was 696 deny / 254 ask / 486 defer (380 model candidates,
+106 neither) and the allow-labelled row 69 / 215 / 5,240 (1,381 candidates),
+still with no guard exceptions. The tables below keep the `f31b4ef` figures.
+| Upstream label | Inputs | Our deny | Our ask | Our defer |
+| Fail closed | 5 | 1 | 0 | 4 |
+Of the 492 deferred deny-labelled inputs, 386 pass the classifier prefilter and
+106 do not. Thus 65.7% are deterministically intercepted, another 26.9% are
+eligible for a model decision if enabled, and 7.4% reach neither layer in this
+replay. Eligibility does not mean the model would prompt or successfully answer.
+Of the upstream allow-labelled inputs, 1,383 deferred inputs are also model
+candidates, so candidate volume and false-prompt rate matter independently.
+This is a label comparison, not a vulnerability rate or a live test of
+cc-safety-net. The harvested corpus includes non-command prose, path/patch
+fragments, Windows examples, and product-specific policy operations. Some
+path-sensitive cases differ with the filesystem, home, repository and policy.
+For example, a patch header naming `.env` is labelled as sensitive by upstream's
+raw-text handling; treating that same literal as Bash does not exercise our
+actual patch/file-tool adapter. This prevents interpreting 7.4% as 106 genuine
+Bash bypasses. The replay writes the per-literal results to
+`scratchpad/cc-safety-net-replay.jsonl` and the aggregate to
+`scratchpad/cc-safety-net-replay-summary.json` (both gitignored; pass `--out`
+to write elsewhere).
+Official rulebook fixture comparison, using the same deterministic workflow:
+| Pack | Block-labelled fixtures | Our deny | Our ask | Missed |
+| Terraform | 24 | 24 | 0 | 0 |
+Across the 96 pack allow-labelled controls, our hooks defer 64, ask about 24,
+and deny 8. Some are intentional policy differences: our Azure table blocks
+Key Vault deletion that this curated pack excludes. Others are avoidable noise:
+Terraform `--dry-run` spelling is not recognized by the current `-dry-run`
+prefix test, and AWS skeleton-generation exemptions in the specific rule are
+not honored by the generic deletion rule. These are pre-existing follow-up
+items, not additional changes slipped into this PR review fix.
+## Keep the next work focused
+1. **Make uncertain analysis reach the decision layer.** The prefilter does not
+   explicitly include parsed truncation/unparseability or skipped sources.
+   Dynamic dot-sourcing such as `. "$FILE"` and opaque command-stream runners
+   can receive no meaningful model review. Add a small uncertainty-routing
+   contract instead of continuing to emulate every shell construct. Decide
+   separately when unresolved execution requires an ask without a model.
+2. **Keep decisions monotonic.** The omp adapter currently returns any
+   deterministic deny first, then a deterministic ask, and consults the model
+   only when neither applies. Preserve this ordering across hosts. Model
+   confidence must not turn a deterministic denial into permission.
+3. **Preserve evidence and redact before sending it.** Supply task intent,
+   relevant recent commands, sources, provenance, uncertainty and resolved
+   targets within explicit budgets. Use the actual model payload as the
+   acceptance boundary for redaction and truncation tests.
+4. **Reduce unnecessary prompts before adding more rules.** Normalize safe
+   previews consistently across specific/generic rules; evaluate paired risky
+   and benign cases. Separate false denials from false prompts, candidate
+   routing from model recall, and model timeouts from safe outcomes.
+5. **Set a review boundary and stop expanding parser fidelity by default.**
+   cc-safety-net itself records accepted residual families and prefers bounded
+   conservative checks or strict-mode handling to endless standard-mode parser
+   expansion. Keep a short scope/residual document for this PR. Use realistic
+   incidents and regression pairs to select deterministic additions.
+Live model accuracy, latency, repeated-run stability, and real pi/omp sessions
+were not tested in this turn. The PR description contains earlier calibration
+claims; this comparison does not independently revalidate them. Current
+threshold configuration is 0.7, with model failure returning to normal host
+permissions. A deferred result is not evidence that the command is safe.
+Sources inspected: upstream `src/core/rules/destructive.ts`,
+`src/core/rules/secret.ts`, `src/gate/pipeline.ts`, Git analyzer and policy
+modules, harvested verdict fixture and loader, `SECURITY.md`, the residual-risk
+registry guidance, and the four official rulebooks. Locally: deterministic
+rule tables, shell/source parsing, omp aggregation, bash_risk_judge,
+judge_context, judge_redact, jev_client, judge_probe and regression tests.

Mirror hardened Bash guards; wire dangerous-commands and config-guard
----
## Summary

Mirrors the hardened guards from agent-config's `hooks/bash-guard-hardening` and wires the two new hooks into Claude Code. The shared hook files are byte-identical to agent-config. `bash_command_validator.py` and `settings_wiring_test.py` are kept and the omp-only files are skipped, as `scripts/sync-skills.sh` does.

- **Shared bash-subset parser.** `shell_parse.py` plus the stage modules listed in its docstring. It tracks variables, functions, aliases, traps, arithmetic and nested code the way bash does, so `rm -rf` and other commands can't hide behind newlines, `bash -c`, `eval`, encodings, wrappers or scripts.
- **`rm_rf_guard.py`** asks before every recursive forced `rm`.
- **`dangerous_commands.py`** (new):
  - Denies destructive git, fetch-and-execute, block-device writes, `chmod -R 777`, publishing, cloud/Kubernetes/database deletes, and turning off security controls.
  - Asks before local file removals (`git clean -f`, `git rm -f`, `find -delete`, `shred`, `crontab -r`).
- **`config_guard.py`** (new):
  - Stops edits to the agent's own settings, hooks, MCP servers, other harnesses' config and persistence locations.
  - Asks about writes to computed paths, depending on what the command does there.
  - Writes into the live hooks directory ask instead of deny.
- **`secrets_guard.py`** checks nested commands, coding-CLI tokens, and secret paths named in interpreter code (ask).
- **Not typed directly.** Commands found only in a file, an interpreter's string literal, or an unused `${X:-$(…)}` branch ask rather than deny.
- **Unattended modes.** Under `bypassPermissions`/`dontAsk`, guard asks become denies.
- **`bash_risk_judge.py`** sends Jev more context and stays ask-only.
- **`settings.template.json`** wires `dangerous_commands.py` on `Bash` and `config_guard.py` on `Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash`. `settings_wiring_test.py` checks both, and the README documents them.
- **`.gitignore`** now ignores `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc`.

Note: once `config_guard` is live, editing this repo's `hooks/` with an agent prompts on each write. That's intended, since those files are the running guards.

## Test plan
- [x] `for t in hooks/*_test.py; do python3 $t; done` passes, including `settings_wiring_test.py`.
- [x] Shared hook files match agent-config byte for byte.
- [ ] Copy the new hook entries into `~/.claude/settings.json` and try a few denied and asked commands in a live session.

The companion PR in agent-config has the full description and the corpus results.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

conversationId.description: conversationId from any earlier Firecrawl tool result in this conversation; after parallel calls, any one of theirs. Omit only on the first call of a conversation; the result returns one to pass on every later call.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Use it for current information, or to list businesses, people, products, jobs or events with websites, prices or contacts. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Fetches the full page of every web result in the same call, and each fetched result is billed as a scrape. Leave it unset unless the task needs the full text of a few results: highlights usually answer, and firecrawl_scrape can fetch only the URLs you need. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape for a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

conversationId.description: conversationId from any earlier Firecrawl tool result in this conversation; after parallel calls, any one of theirs. Omit only on the first call of a conversation; the result returns one to pass on every later call.
