# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web search, page retrieval, site URL discovery, multi-page collection, structured page data, monitoring, and multi-source research that returns structured data. Match the requested operation to the tool boundary: firecrawl_scrape retrieves one supplied page and can return JSON matching a supplied schema, firecrawl_map enumerates URLs under a site without retrieving their content, and firecrawl_agent runs multi-source research and returns structured data when the URLs are not known or the answer spans several sites (an entity plus its fields, a list, a dataset); its result is read with firecrawl_agent_status. Authenticated firecrawl_search returns web results together with matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. Alexandria is Firecrawl's catalogue of data providers and workflows across companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more; providers return typed, sourced records through published contracts. A matching provider can return the same fields across several entities, provenance, exact figures or timestamps, or a large set of records through firecrawl_scrape with its published contract. If web results already answer the question, use them. For the same fields across multiple pages, firecrawl_find_tools offers free provider discovery. Use firecrawl_find_tools to read a contract that was not returned in full or to browse the catalogue by category. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. If no provider fits, continue with web search or firecrawl_agent. For biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature, the firecrawl_research_* tools search a paper index of abstracts and full text; firecrawl_search with categories: ["research"] is a website filter over ordinary web results and reaches different sources. For a programming question (code behaviour, a library or framework, an API contract, an error message, or a known bug), firecrawl_developer_search (or firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"]) searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources and cannot be combined with other categories. firecrawl_search with sources: [{type: "alexandria"}] returns compact tool summaries in data.tools; toolDetail: "full" includes contracts, firecrawl_find_tools starts with categories, lists providers, then compact tools, and expands the selected full contract, and firecrawl_scrape with alexandria: [{provider, capability, options}] executes up to ten capabilities and returns their results. Alexandria access needs an API key on a team with it enabled. Provide only the required inputs and account for stated network or external side effects.

definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session with Alexandria access, `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call. Keyless sessions have no provider matches.

Alexandria mode, on an authenticated session with Alexandria access: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Query operators, domain filters, `categories`, `toolDetail` and `scrapeOptions` are described on their parameters. Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Attach page content for web results in the same call. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape when you need a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

38	equivalent implementation. Eighteen other entries are PowerShell/CMD-specific.
39	The official cloud packs are a separate repository; they are not all enabled by

41	
42	## Measured replay
43	
44	I replayed all 6,965 upstream harvested literals through the four local
45	deterministic hooks, then checked model eligibility only for deferred commands.
46	The saved comparison column is `work/standard`; local checks used an empty
47	workspace, default/high policy, and normal interactive permission mode. No
48	literal was executed, no decision model was called, and there were no guard
49	exceptions. Reproduce from this checkout with:
50	
51	```sh
52	python3 scratchpad/replay_ccsafety.py
53	```
54	
55	| Upstream label | Inputs | Our deny | Our ask | Our defer |
56	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
57	| Deny | 1,436 | 693 (48.3%) | 251 (17.5%) | 492 (34.3%) |
58	| Allow | 5,524 | 70 (1.3%) | 212 (3.8%) | 5,242 (94.9%) |
59	| Fail closed | 5 | 1 | 0 | 4 |
60	
61	Of the 492 deferred deny-labelled inputs, 386 pass the classifier prefilter and
62	106 do not. Thus 65.7% are deterministically intercepted, another 26.9% are
63	eligible for a model decision if enabled, and 7.4% reach neither layer in this
64	replay. Eligibility does not mean the model would prompt or successfully answer.
65	Of the upstream allow-labelled inputs, 1,383 deferred inputs are also model
66	candidates, so candidate volume and false-prompt rate matter independently.
67	
68	This is a label comparison, not a vulnerability rate or a live test of
69	cc-safety-net. The harvested corpus includes non-command prose, path/patch
70	fragments, Windows examples, and product-specific policy operations. Some
71	path-sensitive cases differ with the filesystem, home, repository and policy.
72	For example, a patch header naming `.env` is labelled as sensitive by upstream's
73	raw-text handling; treating that same literal as Bash does not exercise our
74	actual patch/file-tool adapter. This prevents interpreting 7.4% as 106 genuine
75	Bash bypasses. The exact pipeline mismatch data is saved in
76	`cc-safety-net-replay.jsonl` and its aggregate in
77	`cc-safety-net-replay-summary.json`.
78	
79	Official rulebook fixture comparison, using the same deterministic workflow:
80	
81	| Pack | Block-labelled fixtures | Our deny | Our ask | Missed |
82	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
83	| Terraform | 24 | 24 | 0 | 0 |
84	| AWS | 15 | 13 | 2 | 0 |
85	| gcloud | 27 | 27 | 0 | 0 |
86	| Azure | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0 |
87	| Total | 81 | 79 | 2 | 0 |
88	
89	Across the 96 pack allow-labelled controls, our hooks defer 64, ask about 24,
90	and deny 8. Some are intentional policy differences: our Azure table blocks
91	Key Vault deletion that this curated pack excludes. Others are avoidable noise:
92	Terraform `--dry-run` spelling is not recognized by the current `-dry-run`
93	prefix test, and AWS skeleton-generation exemptions in the specific rule are
94	not honored by the generic deletion rule. These are pre-existing follow-up
95	items, not additional changes slipped into this PR review fix.
96	
97	## Keep the next work focused
98	
99	1. **Make uncertain analysis reach the decision layer.** The prefilter does not
100	   explicitly include parsed truncation/unparseability or skipped sources.
101	   Dynamic dot-sourcing such as `. "$FILE"` and opaque command-stream runners
102	   can receive no meaningful model review. Add a small uncertainty-routing
103	   contract instead of continuing to emulate every shell construct. Decide
104	   separately when unresolved execution requires an ask without a model.
105	2. **Keep decisions monotonic.** The omp adapter currently returns any
106	   deterministic deny first, then a deterministic ask, and consults the model
107	   only when neither applies. Preserve this ordering across hosts. Model
108	   confidence must not turn a deterministic denial into permission.
109	3. **Preserve evidence and redact before sending it.** Supply task intent,
110	   relevant recent commands, sources, provenance, uncertainty and resolved
111	   targets within explicit budgets. Use the actual model payload as the
112	   acceptance boundary for redaction and truncation tests.
113	4. **Reduce unnecessary prompts before adding more rules.** Normalize safe
114	   previews consistently across specific/generic rules; evaluate paired risky
115	   and benign cases. Separate false denials from false prompts, candidate
116	   routing from model recall, and model timeouts from safe outcomes.
117	5. **Set a review boundary and stop expanding parser fidelity by default.**
118	   cc-safety-net itself records accepted residual families and prefers bounded
119	   conservative checks or strict-mode handling to endless standard-mode parser
120	   expansion. Keep a short scope/residual document for this PR. Use realistic
121	   incidents and regression pairs to select deterministic additions.
122	
123	Live model accuracy, latency, repeated-run stability, and real pi/omp sessions
124	were not tested in this turn. The PR description contains earlier calibration
125	claims; this comparison does not independently revalidate them. Current
126	threshold configuration is 0.7, with model failure returning to normal host
127	permissions. A deferred result is not evidence that the command is safe.
128

## Summary

Mirrors the hardened guards from agent-config's `hooks/bash-guard-hardening` (jessearmand/agent-config#1, in sync at `79e6e58`) and wires the two new hooks into Claude Code. The shared hook files are byte-identical to agent-config. `bash_command_validator.py` and `settings_wiring_test.py` exist only here; the omp-only files (`omp_guard*.py`) are skipped, as `scripts/sync-skills.sh` does.

- **Shared bash-subset parser.** `shell_parse.py` plus the stage modules listed in its docstring. It tracks variables, functions, aliases, traps, arithmetic and nested code the way bash does, so `rm -rf` and other commands can't hide behind newlines, `bash -c`, `eval`, encodings, wrappers or scripts.
- **`rm_rf_guard.py`** asks before every recursive forced `rm`.
- **`dangerous_commands.py`** (new):
  - Denies destructive git, fetch-and-execute, block-device writes, `chmod -R 777`, publishing, cloud/Kubernetes/database deletes, and turning off security controls.
  - Asks before local file removals (`git clean -f`, `git rm -f`, `find -delete`, `shred`, `crontab -r`).
- **`config_guard.py`** (new):
  - Stops edits to the agent's own settings, hooks, MCP servers, other harnesses' config and persistence locations.
  - Asks about writes to computed paths, depending on what the command does there.
  - Writes into the live hooks directory ask instead of deny.
- **`secrets_guard.py`** checks nested commands, coding-CLI tokens, and secret paths named in interpreter code (ask).
- **Not typed directly.** Commands found only in a file, an interpreter's string literal, or an unused `${X:-$(…)}` branch ask rather than deny.
- **Unattended modes.** Under `bypassPermissions`/`dontAsk`, guard asks become denies.
- **`bash_risk_judge.py`** sends Jev more context and stays ask-only.
- **`settings.template.json`** wires `dangerous_commands.py` on `Bash` and `config_guard.py` on `Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash`. `settings_wiring_test.py` checks both, and the README documents them.
- **`.gitignore`** now ignores `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc`.

Note: once `config_guard` is live, editing this repo's `hooks/` with an agent prompts on each write. That's intended, since those files are the running guards.

## Changes since the first review

Fixes found while reviewing and running the guards live, kept to the existing rules (no new guard families):

- `e2bb198` Bound variable values and a long-word regex so every guard call finishes well inside the 10 s hook timeout (a timed-out hook fails open).
- `19ac272` Catch dash chmod modes (`chmod -w+s`, `chmod 4777 F -s`, `04755`), scripts fed to a shell through `cat` with options, NoSQL `drop()`/`deleteMany({})`, and `python -i`.
- `cf0844e` Compare real paths in the mixed-volume test (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`).
- `6e7996c` Use agent-config's `python_argv.py` as the one Python command-line parser. `python3 -m` maps to the module files Python would load, so `curl … | python3 -m json.tool` is allowed while a downloaded `base64.py` run as `-m base64` is denied.
- Cherry-picked from agent-config:
  - `d9799b3`, `67bc65b`, `d22d61f`: ref mutations, prose credential redaction, and forced `git checkout-index`.
  - `9be210a`: scoped Git, database and publishing review findings.
  - `246acb9`: alternate nested execution forms.
  - `c283cbd`: system persistence trees, and unwrapping `strace`.

## Scope and coverage docs

- `docs/guard-scope.md` sets the review boundary: deterministic guards own the denials, the model may only ask, and parser fidelity is not expanded by default.
- `docs/cc-safety-net-coverage.md` compares coverage with cc-safety-net 2.6.11.
- `scripts/replay_ccsafety.py` reproduces that comparison. It replays upstream's 6,965 harvested literals through the four deterministic guards in-process; nothing is executed and no model is called.

Re-run at `a8d7345`:

| Upstream label | Deny | Ask | Defer | Deferred model candidates |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deny (1,436) | 696 | 254 | 486 | 380 |
| Allow (5,524) | 69 | 215 | 5,240 | 1,381 |
| Fail closed (5) | 1 | 0 | 4 | 0 |

There were no guard exceptions. The doc explains why this is a label comparison, not a bypass rate.

The docs live in `docs/` rather than `hooks/` so that `hooks/` holds only code and a hook sync never touches them. agent-config uses the same layout.

## Test plan

- [x] `for t in hooks/*_test.py; do python3 $t; done` passes, including `settings_wiring_test.py`.
- [x] Shared hook files, both docs and the replay script match agent-config `79e6e58` byte for byte.
- [x] Both hooks are wired into `~/.claude/settings.json` and running live:
  - A 169-case probe through the live hooks gives 0 unexpected results.
  - In real tool calls, `kill -0 1` and a `Write` to `.mcp.json` were denied, and `git reset --hard` and `git checkout <rev> -- <paths>` were blocked.
- [x] A 19-case bypass probe returns deny for every case.
- [x] A replay of about 2,580 commands from past transcripts gives 0 crashes and no call over 1 s.
- [x] Re-ran the replay, which needs the upstream checkout:

  ```sh
  git clone https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net.git scratchpad/cc-safety-net
  git -C scratchpad/cc-safety-net checkout 0626be7a791c17a0daa67ae90a899372c667056d
  python3 scripts/replay_ccsafety.py
  ```

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## cua
Cua Spaces: isolated sandboxes. Any image is a Space; the computer-use and file tools need one that runs cua-spacesd (the Spaces images), and every Space reaches the MCP servers it declares with list_tools/call_tool(service=...). Start with list_spaces; create one with create_space(on="local" (free) or "aws", "gcp" or "modal" (your own cloud account); reuse=true returns a reachable one), or add an existing computer with add_space(url, token). delete_space deletes a Space you created. Then work inside it with space_bash, space_write, upload/send_file/download, and its computer-use tools via list_tools/call_tool. agent_start runs a coding agent inside a Space. Tools marked FOR THE HUMAN draw on the user's own desktop; call them only when asked.

## cua-driver
cua-driver: background GUI automation. No shell: for non-GUI outcomes use an app API/SDK, CLI or filesystem and read the result back there.

1. `list_windows({app:"Name"})` or `launch_app` for `pid` and `window_id`.
2. Read narrowly: `get_window_state` with `query:"Save"`. Re-read with `since:"latest"`.
3. Act by `element_token` (AX): row `[N]` is `<snapshot_id>:N`. Pixels only for surfaces missing from the tree.
4. Act through `run_steps({steps:[{tool,args}],observe:{}})`, even for one step: stops at the first failure, returns what changed. Loops, branches or retries: one `run_script` call.
5. Verify at checkpoints, not after every action: `verify_state(pid, window_id, expect)`. `unknown` and `effect:"unverifiable"` are not success.

Use the narrowest semantic route first: `set_window_frame` plus `list_windows` for geometry, typed browser tools for pages. Stay in the background; `delivery_mode:"foreground"` only if refused or unverifiable.

Chrome/Edge/Brave page: `get_browser_state({pid, window_id})`, its `detail.next_call` (`browser_prepare`) if refused, then `browser_click`/`browser_type`/`browser_pointer` (hover, drag); never desktop pointer tools.

`start_session` is optional; repeat a short `session` label on every call that accepts it. On continuation/recent-work, call `history_status`; if ready, make one bounded initial `history_query` before broad discovery.

Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

conversationId.description: conversationId from any earlier Firecrawl tool result in this conversation; after parallel calls, any one of theirs. Omit only on the first call of a conversation; the result returns one to pass on every later call.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Use it for current information, or to list businesses, people, products, jobs or events with websites, prices or contacts. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Fetches the full page of every web result in the same call, and each fetched result is billed as a scrape. Leave it unset unless the task needs the full text of a few results: highlights usually answer, and firecrawl_scrape can fetch only the URLs you need. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape for a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

conversationId.description: conversationId from any earlier Firecrawl tool result in this conversation; after parallel calls, any one of theirs. Omit only on the first call of a conversation; the result returns one to pass on every later call.

# claude-decisions-mod

A [Claude Code mod](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) that
decides, before a tool call runs, whether it may: deterministic guards for the
Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep and Glob tools, and a model-assisted second
opinion from a **decision model** ([Jev](https://vercel.com/kb/jev-from-typesafe-ai)
by TypeSafe AI on [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/modalities/decision))
for the long tail of risky commands no rule enumerates.

It is the TypeScript port of the Python hooks in
[`jessearmand/claude-code-rules`](https://github.com/jessearmand/claude-code-rules)
(`hooks/*.py`), rewritten as a hooks module that runs inside Claude Code
instead of as settings-hook scripts. Policy, rule ids, reason texts and the
bash-subset parser are the same; see [docs/PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md) for
the module map and the conventions of the port.

[cc-safety-net](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net) is the reference for
guard-family coverage. PowerShell and Windows shells are out of scope: the
guards cover Bash on Linux and macOS.

## Install

At the prompt of a Claude Code terminal session:

```
/plugin install decisions-guard --marketplace jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod
```

From a shell:

```
claude plugin install decisions-guard --marketplace jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod
```

In the Desktop app, where `/plugin` does not run: click **+** next to the
prompt box, then **Plugins**, **Add marketplace** with
`jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod`, then **Add plugin**.

To run it from a checkout for one session: `claude --plugin-dir /path/to/claude-decisions-mod`.

Do not also wire the Python hooks of `claude-code-rules` in `settings.json`:
every call would be judged twice.

## What it decides

Every guard answers `deny` or `ask` or defers to the normal permission flow;
none ever answers `allow`, so your own permission rules are never loosened.
A deny from any guard wins over an ask; the model is consulted only when
nothing deterministic decided, and it can only ask.

| Guard | Tools | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rm-rf-guard` | Bash | Asks before any `rm` that is both recursive and forced, with a per-target analysis and the least destructive alternative. Removals entirely inside a `scratchpad` directory of the project (symlinks followed) do not ask: the agent manages those. |
| `dangerous-commands` | Bash | Denies (or asks about) destructive git, downloads piped into a shell, disk writes, `chmod -R 777`, crontab, package publishing, cloud/Kubernetes/database deletes and switching off security controls. Local removals (`git clean -f`, `find -delete`, `shred`) ask. |
| `secrets-guard` | Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob | Blocks reading, mutating or exfiltrating credential files (`.env`, keys, cloud and coding-agent tokens), in three tiers. |
| `config-guard` | Bash, Edit, Write | Stops the agent changing its own settings, hooks, MCP servers, other harnesses' config, home-directory skills and instructions, and persistence locations (shell rc files, git hooks and config, launchd, systemd, cron). |
| `file-protection` | Edit, Write | Denies hand edits to generated files: lockfiles, `.git/` internals, `node_modules/`. |
| `bash-command-validator` | Bash | Points `grep`, `find -name` and source-code `rg` at `rg`, `rg --files` and `ast-grep`. |
| `bash-risk-judge` | Bash | Opt-in. Asks a decision model typed questions (destruction, exfiltration, persistence, weakened controls, fetch-and-execute, privilege escalation, erased history, credential stores, network exposure, off-task) and prompts when any crosses a threshold. |

All Bash guards parse the command with a shared bash-subset parser, so
newlines, `sudo -u x`, `timeout 5`, `bash -c`, `eval`, `ssh host '...'`,
`$(...)`, heredocs fed to a shell and interpreter one-liners cannot hide a
command, and what a command runs from disk (shell scripts, `npm run`
scripts, Makefile recipes, database command files, git aliases) is read and
judged too. A match found only in such a file asks instead of denying.

Under `bypassPermissions` or `dontAsk`, where nobody can answer, a
deterministic ask becomes a deny (set `unattendedKeepAsk` to keep asks).
The mode is read from the merged settings' `permissions.defaultMode`.

## The Jev risk judge

The judge is off until enabled. It sends the (redacted) command, the
user's latest prompt, the agent's last few commands and the body of any
script the command runs to `POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/evaluate`
with typed boolean and choice questions, and reads back calibrated
probabilities. Credentials are, in order: `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`,
`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, the `jevApiKey` option, or `fnox` (pointed at
`HOOK_JEV_FNOX_CONFIG`). Every failure (no key, timeout, bad JSON) defers.

Any gateway decision model works in place of Jev, for example
`openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions`.

## Configuration

Options are set in `/plugin configure decisions-guard@claude-decisions-mod`
(or `claude plugin configure`) and stored in `settings.json` under
`pluginConfigs`. The Python hooks' environment variables are honoured as
overrides, so an existing `env` block keeps working. When an environment
variable replaces an option you set to a different value (for example
`askThreshold` 0.75 under `BASH_RISK_JUDGE_ASK_THRESHOLD=0.6`), the mod
says so when the session starts.

| Option | Environment | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jevEnable` | `HOOK_JEV_ENABLE` | off | Turn the judge on. |
| `jevModel` | `HOOK_JEV_MODEL` | `typesafe-ai/jev` | Gateway decision model id. |
| `jevApiKey` | `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` / `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` | | Gateway credential (stored in secure storage). |
| `jevTimeoutSeconds` | `HOOK_JEV_TIMEOUT` | 5 | Deadline for the decision call. |
| `askThreshold` | `BASH_RISK_JUDGE_ASK_THRESHOLD` | 0.7 | Probability at or above which the judge asks. |
| `secretsLevel` | `SECRETS_GUARD_LEVEL` | `high` | `critical`, `high` or `strict`. |
| `dangerousLevel` | `DANGEROUS_COMMANDS_LEVEL` | `high` | `critical`, `high` or `strict`. |
| `askInsteadOfDeny` | `*_ASK`, `HOOK_ASK_<LEVEL>` | off | Prompt instead of denying. |
| `unattendedKeepAsk` | `HOOK_UNATTENDED_KEEP_ASK` | off | Keep asks under `bypassPermissions`/`dontAsk`. |
| `logDir` | `HOOKS_LOG_DIR`, `*_LOG_DIR` | `~/.claude/hooks-logs` | Audit log directory (JSONL, one file a day). |

Each guard also has a `*_DISABLE` environment switch
(`RM_RF_GUARD_DISABLE`, `DANGEROUS_COMMANDS_DISABLE`, `SECRETS_GUARD_DISABLE`,
`CONFIG_GUARD_DISABLE`, `FILE_PROTECTION_DISABLE`,
`BASH_COMMAND_VALIDATOR_DISABLE`, `BASH_RISK_JUDGE_DISABLE`), and
`CONFIG_GUARD_LIVE_DIRS`, `BASH_RISK_JUDGE_CONTEXT`,
`BASH_RISK_JUDGE_TRUST_TRUNCATED`, `BASH_RISK_JUDGE_UNATTENDED_DENY`,
`HOOK_JEV_DEBUG` and `HOOK_JEV_GATEWAY_URL` keep their Python meaning.

## Development

```
bun install
bun run typecheck   # tsc against the engine's types and against Node
bun run lint        # oxlint + oxfmt --check
bun run format      # oxfmt --write (lint:fix also applies oxlint fixes)
bun run test        # vitest: the ported Python corpora and parity fixtures
bun run test:mod    # claude plugin test: the hooks module against the engine
bun run validate    # claude plugin validate
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs every command above except `format`;
`lint` already fails on unformatted code. The engine's types in
`.claude-plugin/types/` are committed so CI can type-check the hooks module,
and CI installs the Claude Code version named on their first line. Claude Code
rewrites that file when it loads the mod after an update: commit the new
version so CI moves to it.

### Parity with the Python hooks

The port is checked against the Python hooks three ways:

- Every Python test corpus runs as a vitest spec (7,648 tests), and the
  parser modules compare their output on about 1,000 corpus commands with
  fixtures the Python modules generated (`scripts/parity/gen-*-fixture.py`).
- `scripts/replay-ccsafety.ts` replays cc-safety-net's 6,965 harvested
  verdict labels (upstream commit `0626be7a`) through the four deterministic
  guards in-process and, with `--compare`, diffs each literal's decision,
  per-guard verdicts and judge eligibility against the Python replay
  (`python3 scripts/replay_ccsafety.py` in `claude-code-rules`). At the
  time of the port the two agree on all 6,965 rows: 695 deny, 255 ask and
  486 defer on upstream's deny label; 70, 213 and 5,241 on its allow label.
- `scripts/judge-probe.ts` and `scripts/jev-calibrate.ts` are the Python
  probe and calibration harnesses. They need network access and a gateway
  credential; they are benchmarks, not tests.

## Where it runs

Hooks run wherever the plugin loads: the terminal, the Desktop app's Code
tab, the VS Code extension, `claude -p` and cloud sessions that carry the
plugin. `classic.PreToolUse` hooks of a user-installed plugin do not run
where an organization manages Claude Code; an administrator lists the plugin
in managed settings instead.

- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
